A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhiNet/X-PhiNet research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, online-learning and continual-learning experiments in Section 5 and Appendices E–F, including accuracy, forgetting, ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds VOC detection-transfer results, augmentation controls, fast/slow encoder comparisons and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The encoders, two predictors, combined losses and EMA extension remain the same. The corrected EMA equation in Section 3.2 matches the slow-encoder update already present in v1 Listing 2. The newly specified Tanh output activation adds implementation detail without establishing that the architecture actually changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds object-detection transfer evaluation using VOC 07 and VOC 07+12 in Appendix E.5 and Table 14. This substantially broadens task coverage beyond v1's classification and online/continual representation-learning evaluations, which are retained.

E2.justification: MoCo v2 participates in the new detection comparison in Table 14, and MoCo appears in Table 15's weight-decay comparison. The existing SimSiam, BYOL, Barlow Twins and RM-SimSiam comparisons remain. CaSSLe is newly discussed but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added detection evaluation introduces AP50, AP and AP75 measurements and two pretraining recipes: learning rate/weight decay of 0.05/1e-4 and 0.5/1e-5. New controls also compare augmentation of the original-input branch and evaluation of fast versus EMA encoders. The established classification and continual-learning protocols are largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive tests of central design choices: augmentation of the third input on CIFAR-5m and CIFAR10, an identity-predictor comparison on CIFAR-5m, and fast-versus-slow encoder trajectories in Figure 9. The STL10 early-training curves and predictor stable-rank analysis already existed in v1 and are not new analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds error bars to the CIFAR10 robustness curves displayed without them in v1 Figure 5. Existing three-seed statements and tabulated mean/variance reporting are retained. No increase in run count is established, and the added error bars are not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: v2 adds detection, augmentation, encoder-comparison and timing results. For example, Table 14 newly reports VOC 07+12 AP of 55.1 for SimSiam, 56.8 for PhiNet and 56.9 for X-PhiNet under the 0.05/1e-4 recipe. These are new evaluations; the main Tables 1–2 and retained appendix benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-linear assumptions, matrix and eigenvalue dynamics, eigenspace-alignment argument and adiabatic-elimination derivation are retained. v2 Appendix B adds the discrete-update interpretation of the existing gradient flow and a scalarization explanation, without changing the mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The four listed contributions remain substantially unchanged. However, v2 makes investigating the temporal prediction hypothesis an explicit central aim and concludes that robustness and adaptivity corroborate it. v1 more cautiously said the dynamics analysis might partially support biological plausibility.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the slower EMA encoder as regularization for past samples and suggests that regularization imbalance might explain weaker results when all inputs are augmented. It also explicitly attributes early-training stabilization to regularization. The backpropagation, recurrence and loss-choice limitations were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a PhiNets repository link, corrects the EMA equation, reports training times in Table 18, and distinguishes predictor g's hidden ReLU from its output Tanh in Tables 19–20. v1 already supplied extensive settings, hardware information and pseudocode; the additions refine that documentation.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions the work as a computational investigation of temporal prediction, replacing much of the earlier backpropagation and brain-architecture framing. Related work adds MoCo, CaSSLe and video predictive-learning literature and corrects DualNet's fast/slow learning roles. The updated Chen citation represents the same hippocampal work, not a new reference.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, related-work explanations and subsection titles are revised, and an existing limitations summary is brought into the main text. The broader-impacts section is removed, while the appendices are reorganized and numerous language errors are corrected.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout, adds a SimSiam architecture panel, separates the hippocampal interpretation diagram, and moves the existing STL10 curves into the main text. It redraws the robustness plot with error bars and revised axes/legends, expands Table 3, and adds encoder/augmentation figures and transfer/timing tables.

improvement.justification: The added augmentation and fast/slow encoder controls better test central design explanations, while VOC results broaden transfer evidence. Corrected EMA documentation, activation details and the repository link improve reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains over v1's extensive evaluation, tempered by incomplete transfer-protocol reporting, particularly Table 15's unspecified metric, and stronger biological conclusions without direct biological validation.
